title: Arjuna Stands Up
hook: eighteen chapters later, Arjuna's confusion is gone, and the week comes back
carry: karma yoga: act fully, offer the fruit
tomorrow: why is there a stick in the middle of Nani's line?

segments.voice: Yesterday, svadhyaya: holy study goes with a guide, and Priya let Nani be hers. Today the week comes back, and so does Arjuna.

Eighteen chapters after his bow slipped from his hand, Arjuna is still in the chariot between two armies, with Krishna holding the reins. Krishna has finished teaching. And he asks one last question: have you heard all this with a focused mind? Is your confusion gone?
screen: `EIGHTEEN CHAPTERS LATER.` → `HAVE YOU HEARD?` → `IS YOUR CONFUSION GONE?`

segments.voice: Arjuna answers: my confusion is gone. By your grace I remember. My doubts have fallen away. I will do as you say. The Gita ends there; the epic goes on, and Arjuna fights. Walk back through the week and you can see what changed him. Day one, karma yoga: his right is to the action, never to its fruits. Then Maitreyi, turning down a fortune to ask about the atman, the Self that makes anything dear. Then shruti: holy words heard first, written later, Ganesha holding the pen for Vyasa. Then Shabari's tasted berries and bhakti: offer the fruit with love, and God accepts it. Then abhyasa, the restless mind held by coming back, bead by bead. Then svadhyaya: study with someone who has lived inside it. Put together, it's one way of life: act fully, offer what comes of it, know who you really are, keep coming back, and learn it from someone. Priya's card sits on her desk with half of Nani's line inside: karmany evadhikaras te, ma phaleshu kadachana. Your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits. Even the marks hold the week: the knot in karma, the curl in adhi, the e and the u of phaleshu. A week ago it was squiggles. Now she knows she isn't writing it to make Nani cry. She's writing it as an offering. What Nani does with it is the fruit.
screen: `MY CONFUSION IS GONE.` · `KARMA YOGA. ATMAN. SHRUTI.` · `BHAKTI. ABHYASA. SVADHYAYA.` · `ACT FULLY. OFFER THE FRUIT.` · then, large: `THE CARD IS AN OFFERING.`

segments.voice: Say the half line aloud, slowly, one piece per breath out: karmany, evadhikaras te, ma phaleshu, kadachana. Don't worry about getting it perfect. Then bring to mind whatever you'll do next. If you pray, offer it now, before you begin; if you don't, simply hold it lightly, without its fruit. Sit in the quiet after.
Devanagari, once more: the script of Nani's line, and a week of teachings in half a line of it.
For the road: karma yoga. Act fully, offer the fruit, let it go. A week, done.

howItsDone: Students often learn a Gita verse by copying it out by hand and reciting it with a teacher, half a line at a time, until it can be said from memory; many temples and families recite the Gita together on Gita Jayanti.

chat.says: HALF THE LINE IS IN THE CARD 😭 but what if Nani doesn't even notice it at the party??

chat.meaning: The line in the card is Krishna's: your right is to the action, never to its fruits. The card is the offering; Nani's reaction is the fruit.

tie.story: Arjuna, who had dropped his bow, told Krishna at the Gita's end that his confusion was gone and he would act.
tie.friend: Priya can give the card as an offering and let Nani's reaction be the fruit.
tie.you: what could you offer this week instead of gripping?

karma.meaning: action; the root of karmany, the first word of the Gita's line

phaleshu.meaning: in the fruits; from the Gita's line about action

kadachana.meaning: ever, at any time; with ma, 'never'

Nani.meaning: a mother's mother; in Hindi, grandma

Arjuna.meaning: the warrior Krishna teaches in the Gita

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 2.47, first half (karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana)

notes: Review shape: recall holds six of the week's words (the short i, virama, phaleshu, conjunct, abhyasa, svadhyaya). Teaches Devanagari lightly as a system. Answers 1434's question.

Gita 2.47's first half is given in transliteration and paraphrased ('your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits'); no translation quoted. Check the claim that it has no virama in standard Devanagari printings (कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन): it has none; confirm.
'Adhi' here is the syllables a-dhi of adhikara (धि). 'The line was in Nani's book and on her lips long before it was in this card' refers to Priya's storyline.

Priya storyline (v3, days 1427-1442, picked up from 1427-1428): Nani's birthday is two weeks out and Priya is learning Devanagari to handwrite Nani's favorite line, Bhagavad Gita 2.47, in a card; mid-arc Sam wants a Sanskrit tattoo for graduation, Priya is too harsh about it and mends it; at the birthday Nani says the line by heart.
